results.title: Python 3.13: Blazing New Trails in Performance and Scale - The New Stack
results.content:
As noted, some of the major changes to Python include a new interactive interpreter, as well as experimental support for running in a free-threaded mode and a JIT compiler.

## Free Threading [...] Historically, Python’s GIL prevented true concurrent execution of threads, Stanley Seibert, senior director of Community Innovation at Anaconda, told The New Stack. However, the new experimental feature in Python 3.13 allows for concurrent execution of pure Python code. The feature aims to better utilize multicore processors without sacrificing single-thread performance. It will be turned off by default in this release due to its experimental nature. The feature was developed by Meta engineers [...] Andrew Cornwall, an analyst at Forrester Research, agrees that the two most significant runtime changes in Python 3.13 are experimental, “so everyday CPython users won’t see much difference yet,” he told The New Stack. However, Python is laying the groundwork for faster code running on multiple processors.

results.title: What’s New In Python 3.13 — Python 3.15.0 documentation
results.content: Python 3.13 is a stable release of the Python programming language, with a mix of changes to the language, the implementation and the standard library. The biggest changes include a new interactive interpreter, experimental support for running in a free-threaded mode (PEP 703), and a Just-In-Time compiler (PEP 744). [...] CPython now has experimental support for running in a free-threaded mode, with the global interpreter lock (GIL) disabled. This is an experimental feature and therefore is not enabled by default. The free-threaded mode requires a different executable, usually called `python3.13t` or `python3.13t.exe`. Pre-built binaries marked as free-threaded can be installed as part of the official Windows and macOS installers, or CPython can be built from source with the `--disable-gil` option. [...] `multiprocessing`: The default start method will change to a safer one on Linux, BSDs, and other non-macOS POSIX platforms where `'fork'` is currently the default (gh-84559). Adding a runtime warning about this was deemed too disruptive as the majority of code is not expected to care. Use the `get_context()` or `set_start_method()` APIs to explicitly specify when your code requires `'fork'`. See Contexts and start methods.

## 6️⃣ Python 3.13 — The Bigger Architectural Shift

Now we move into more interesting territory.

### 🧵 PEP 703 — GIL-Free Python (Experimental)

This is historic. PEP 703 introduces a build configuration that removes the Global Interpreter Lock.

Important:

 It is optional.
 Not default (yet).
 Significant ecosystem changes required.

### Why GIL Removal is Hard

The GIL protects:

 Reference counting
 Memory management
 Object model consistency

Removing it requires: [...] ## 5️⃣ CPython Interpreter Internals Evolution

### Adaptive Specialization (Carried from 3.11 → Refined in 3.12)

CPython now modifies bytecode at runtime.

Instead of static opcodes like:

```
LOAD_ATTR LOAD_ATTR
```

It adapts to:

```
LOAD_ATTR_INSTANCE_VALUE LOAD_ATTR_INSTANCE_VALUE
```

If it detects:

 Stable object types
 Predictable attribute layout

This reduces dictionary lookups.

### Think of it like:

A lightweight runtime JIT without full compilation. [...] You may observe:

 Smaller layers
 Faster startup
 Better dependency resolution

Combine with:

 Multi-stage builds
 Distroless runtime images
 Non-root execution

Python is no longer:

 “Slow scripting language”
 “Single-threaded only”

It is evolving into:

 A performance-aware runtime
 Cloud-native friendly platform
 Concurrency-optimized ecosystem

The interpreter itself is becoming smarter.

results.title: Everything you need to know about Python 3.13 – JIT and GIL went up the hill | Drew's Dev Blog
results.content:
In short, there are two big changes being made to how Python runs at a core level which have the potential to radically change the performance profile of Python code in the future.

Those changes are:

 A “free-threaded” version of CPython which allows you to disable the Global Interpreter Lock (GIL), and
 Support for experimental Just-in-Time (JIT) compilation.

So what are these new features and what impact will they have on you?

## Global Interpreter Lock (GIL)

### What is the GIL? [...] Phase 1: Free-threading mode is an experimental build-time option that is not the default.
 Phase 2: Free-threading mode is officially supported but still not the default.
 Phase 3: Free-threading mode is the default. [...] `3.13.0rc2t-g1` – the Python 3.13.0 release candidate 2 with experimental free-threading enabled at build-time, run with the `-X gil=1` argument, thereby “re-enabling” the GIL at runtime.

results.content:
No. Each Rhino version is fixed to a single Python 3 runtime version. This is what almost any other application that supports Python scripting does as well. We might consider adding an optional Experimental package to support newer or older python versions if there is a solid reason for it.

#### Is Rhino 9 going to ship with Python 3.13.3?

No. We will keep updating the runtime to newer patches e.g. 3.13.10 during the Rhino WIP life time, but Rhino 9 should remain fixed to Python 3.13.x [...] Just install Rhino BETA and open ScriptEditor like before. It will deploy then new python runtime under `~/.rhinocode/py313-rh9` folder. We have also updated pythonnet to v3.0.5 since it is the latest version and has recently added support for Python 3.13

`~/.rhinocode/py313-rh9`

We have also improved error reporting when language initialization fails. Clicking on the error now opens the logs window with information on how to report the bug: [...] #### How does it affect my scripts or published plugins?

There should not be any changes needed to be done to your scripts. Any script with `#! python 3` directive or `.py3` file extension will automatically choose the new runtime. This includes Grasshopper python 3 scripts as well as any other scripts you run using Rhino command prompt.
